title: Prevalence of alpha-synuclein seeding activity in the Olfactory Mucosa following SARS-CoV-2 infection: results from a pilot study
title_zh: SARS‑CoV‑2感染后嗅黏膜中α‑突触核蛋白诱导活性流行率：一项试点研究结果
abstract: Abstract Olfactory dysfunction (OD) is a hallmark of SARS-CoV-2-infection where it is believed to result from neuroinflammation induced by viral invasion via the olfactory mucosa (OM). Hyposmia also affects the majority of patients with Parkinson’s disease (PD) where it is caused by α-synuclein (aSyn) pathology in the olfactory system, and aSyn-seeding-activity can be detected in the OM using aSyn-seeding-amplification-assays (aSyn-SAA). The present pilot study aimed to investigate whether SARS-CoV-2-infection induces local aSyn-misfolding and -aggregation in OM samples using aSyn-SAA. We conducted an observational study including PD patients (n = 51), individuals with a history of documented symptomatic SARS-CoV-2-infection (post-COVID; n = 95), and healthy controls (HC; n = 42). Post-COVID-participants were stratified based on persistent OD (COVID+OD; n = 42) or normal olfaction (COVID–OD; n = 53) using Sniffin’-Sticks-Identification (SSI) and -Discrimination (SSD) tests. OM samples were obtained by ENT specialists and analyzed by aSyn-SAA at the University of Verona. Clinical phenotyping included MDS-UPDRS, MoCA, and the Innsbruck-RBD-Inventory. OM-SAA positivity rates were significantly different between PD and both post-COVID-participants and HCs (80.4% vs 24.2% vs 11.9%; p < 0.001). Within the post-COVID-group, positivity rates were higher in COVID+OD vs COVID–OD (35.7% vs 15.1%; p = 0.030), and COVID+OD differed from HC ( p = 0.030), while COVID–OD did not ( p = 0.65). Among post-COVID-participants, aSyn-SAA positivity was associated with lower SSI ( p = 0.007) and SSD ( p < 0.001) scores, but not with MDS-UPDRS, MoCA, or RBD measures. OM-SAA-positivity was enriched among individuals with persistent post-COVID-OD and correlated with olfactory impairment. These findings support the hypothesis that neuroinflammation following SARS-COV-2-infection might promote local aSyn-aggregation. The biological and prognostic relevance of OM-SAA positivity is unknown and needs further prospective investigation.
abstract_zh: 摘要 嗅觉功能障碍（OD）是SARS‑CoV‑2感染的标志性症状，据信其源于病毒通过嗅黏膜（OM）侵袭引起的神经炎症。嗅觉减退也影响大多数帕金森病（PD）患者，其原因是嗅觉系统中α‑突触核蛋白（aSyn）病理，且可通过aSyn‑诱导放大测定（aSyn‑SAA）在OM中检测到aSyn诱导活性。本试点研究旨在探讨SARS‑CoV‑2感染是否导致OM样本中aSyn错误折叠和聚集。我们进行了一项观察性研究，纳入PD患者（n=51）、有记录的症状性SARS‑CoV‑2感染史（后COVID；n=95）以及健康对照（HC；n=42）。后COVID受试者根据持续OD（COVID+OD；n=42）或正常嗅觉（COVID‑OD；n=53）进行分层，使用Sniffin’‑Sticks识别（SSI）和辨别（SSD）测试。OM样本由耳鼻喉科医生采集，并在维罗纳大学使用aSyn‑SAA进行分析。临床表型包括MDS‑UPDRS、MoCA和因斯布鲁克RBD清单。OM‑SAA阳性率在PD与后COVID受试者及HC之间显著不同（80.4% vs 24.2% vs 11.9%；p<0.001）。在后COVID组内，COVID+OD的阳性率高于COVID‑OD（35.7% vs 15.1%；p=0.030），且COVID+OD与HC显著差异（p=0.030），而COVID‑OD无显著差异（p=0.65）。在后COVID受试者中，aSyn‑SAA阳性与SSI（p=0.007）和SSD（p<0.001）得分降低相关，但与MDS‑UPDRS、MoCA或RBD测量无关。OM‑SAA阳性在持续后COVID OD个体中更为丰富，并与嗅觉受损相关。这些发现支持神经炎症在SARS‑CoV‑2感染后可能促进局部aSyn聚集的假设。OM‑SAA阳性的生物学和预后意义尚不清楚，需要进一步的前瞻性研究。
